close_reason: Resolved as Path B (document why) per the bead's own 'if unchanged, document why in the rustdoc' instruction. Path A (HashMap<Id, _>) would require either accepting non-deterministic JSON output (breaks snapshot tests) or adding Ord to Id in jmap-types (workspace-wide canonical-template propagation pass). The runtime duplicate-accountId check is small, shared via build_chat_push_map, and unit-tested. Rustdoc on PushSubscriptionCreateInput.chat_push explains the trade-off.
description: src/methods/mod.rs:1163-1180. chat_push: Option<&'a [(&'a Id, jmap_chat_types::ChatPushConfig)]>. The wire format is a JSON object mapping accountId → ChatPushConfig; the slice-of-tuple shape forces callers to construct Vec<(Id, ChatPushConfig)> first, and makes the runtime duplicate-accountId check in misc.rs:230-240 necessary. A &HashMap<Id, ChatPushConfig> or a dedicated newtype would eliminate the runtime check. Trade-off: requires &HashMap argument lifetimes to work; not all callers may have one ready. Consider whether the ergonomic loss outweighs the type-safety win. If unchanged, document why in the rustdoc.
title: PushSubscriptionCreateInput.chat_push uses tuple slice instead of HashMap
